### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

compiler

### Description

Follow-up to the discussion in #70514, filed as agreed there.

Since #70188, templates can access members declared `private` on the component class. The motivation given in #70188 is specific: under `isolatedDeclarations: true`, template-facing members declared `protected` require explicit type annotations, and allowing `private` removes that requirement. The behaviour change, however, applies to every Angular component, whether or not `isolatedDeclarations` is used.

For existing codebases this lands implicitly. On upgrade, every `private` member already written becomes reachable from the template at once. Nothing breaks at runtime, but the boundary a declaration expresses and the boundary the compiler enforces no longer match, and they stay mismatched until the codebase has been migrated to whatever the new convention is. There is no diagnostic to surface this, and the style guide still recommends `protected` for template-facing members.

JS `#private` elements remain inaccessible from templates, but only because of a runtime limitation. If class and template are meant to be one cohesive unit, that argument covers `#private` too, so it is not clear this is a boundary teams should build on. A related question raised in #70514 is whether, with the TypeScript 7 compiler, `.ngtypecheck.ts` files are still generated in the same way, which also bears on how stable the current behaviour is.

As it stands, upgrading to 22.2 and committing to a new convention for member visibility cannot be separated. An option would let them happen in that order, on the team's own schedule.

### Proposed solution

An `angularCompilerOptions` flag that controls whether templates may access `private` members. Following @PapaNappa's suggestion in #70514:

```jsonc
"angularCompilerOptions": {
  // "auto" (default) | "allow" | "disallow"
  "privateAccessFromTemplates": "auto"
}
```

- `auto` derives the behaviour from `isolatedDeclarations`: allowed when it is enabled, disallowed when it is not. This keeps the benefit for the codebases the change was aimed at, and leaves the previous semantics in place elsewhere.
- `allow` and `disallow` let a team opt in or out explicitly, independently of `isolatedDeclarations`.

@PowerKiKi suggested a simpler variant: no new flag, and template access to `private` members permitted only when `isolatedDeclarations` is enabled. That would also address the problem, at the cost of not being separately controllable.

A lighter alternative would be an opt-in diagnostic that reports template access to `private` members, leaving the behaviour unchanged. That is enough to keep a convention enforceable, though it does not restore the previous semantics.

### Alternatives considered

**Migrate template-facing members to `private` and hidden members to `#private`.** This is the smallest change, and mostly automatable. It depends on `#private` remaining inaccessible from templates, which is not documented. It also has known friction: `#private` members cannot be reached from tests the way `private` ones can via `component['member']`, and `private` members used only in templates are reported as unused (TS6133).

**Move anything the template must not reach off the component**, into an injected ViewModel, Facade or Store. This keeps the boundary regardless of how member visibility is treated, but it is a design change in every affected component rather than a rename, and it is disproportionate for small components.

**Adopt the new behaviour as is.** Viable for new code. For an existing codebase it means accepting a mismatch between declared and enforced visibility across the whole codebase for the duration of the migration, with no tooling to track progress.

**An external lint rule.** Angular ESLint could in principle flag template access to `private` members. This would live outside the compiler and could drift from its semantics, and it does not help teams that do not use it.

### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? compiler-cli, language-service ### Is this a regression? No ### Description Since #70188 (22.2.0), a template can read `private` members of its component. TypeScript doesn't see those reads though, so a `private` member that is only used in the template is still reported as unused (TS6133). ```ts import {Component, signal} from '@angular/core'; @Component({ selector: 'app-root', template: `

{{ privateTitle() }}

{{ protectedTitle() }}

`, }) export class App { private readonly privateTitle = signal('private member'); protected readonly protectedTitle = signal('protected member'); } ``` With `"noUnusedLocals": true` in `tsconfig.json`, `ng build` fails: ``` ✘ [ERROR] TS6133: 'privateTitle' is declared but its value is never read. [plugin angular-compiler] src/app.ts:12:19: 12 │ private readonly privateTitle = signal('private member'); ╵ ~~~~~~~~~~~~ ``` `ng serve` fails the same way on startup. Without `noUnusedLocals` the build passes, but the editor still greys out `privateTitle` and offers the "Remove unused declaration for: 'privateTitle'" quick fix, which breaks the template when applied. The Angular language service forwards TypeScript's suggestion diagnostics as is, so having the extension installed doesn't change this. `protectedTitle` isn't reported in either case, since TypeScript doesn't track unused `protected` members. I'd expect a `private` member read by the component's own template to count as used, both in the build and in the editor. Whatever the fix, private members that are genuinely unused should still be reported, since that's what `noUnusedLocals` is for. This came up in https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/70514#issuecomment-5813840954, opening a separate issue so it can be tracked on its own. ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug The component above, with `"noUnusedLocals": true` in `tsconfig.json`. ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```true TS6133: 'privateTitle' is declared but its value is never read. ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```true Angular CLI : 22.2.0 Angular : 22.2.0 Node.js : 24.21.0 Package Manager : npm 11.19.0 Operating System : darwin arm64 ┌───────────────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────────┐ │ Package │ Installed Version │ Requested Version │ ├───────────────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────────┤ │ @angular/build │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/cli │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/common │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/compiler │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/compiler-cli │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/core │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/platform-browser │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ rxjs │ 7.8.2 │ ~7.8.0 │ │ typescript │ 6.0.3 │ ~6.0.2 │ └───────────────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────────────────┘ ``` ### Anything else? _No response_

body_text: ### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? compiler ### Is this a regression? Yes ### Description A library compiled with Angular < 22 in partial compilation mode (`ɵɵngDeclareComponent({ version: "20.3.x", ... })`) whose component omits `changeDetection` is handled differently by the two consumers of that declaration in an Angular 22 application: - **AOT (partial linker)** keeps it on `Default`/`Eager`: `packages/compiler-cli/linker/src/file_linker/partial_linkers/partial_component_linker_1.ts` computes `hasOnPushByDefault = major >= 22 || version === PLACEHOLDER_VERSION` and only then falls back to `OnPush`. That is correct: a component written for v20 was always checked and may assign state inside subscriptions or callbacks without `markForCheck()`. - **JIT (`ɵɵngDeclareComponent` → `ɵcompilerFacade.compileComponentDeclaration`)** ignores the declared version: `packages/compiler/src/jit_compiler_facade.ts`, `convertDeclareComponentFacadeToMetadata`, uses `changeDetection: decl.changeDetection ?? ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush`. The same v20 component becomes `OnPush` and silently stops re-rendering. JIT is what Storybook (`@storybook/angular`), Jest (`jest-preset-angular`), Vitest without the AOT plugin, `TestBed` and `ng serve --aot=false` use, so a library that works in the built application breaks in every one of those. We hit it with Kendo UI for Angular 25 (compiled with Angular 20.3): its internal `TreeViewGroupComponent` assigns nodes inside a subscription and rendered an empty tree in Storybook, while the AOT build was fine. This is the declare-path counterpart of #70262. That issue is about the JIT *decorator* path (`@Component` metadata → `Eager`) diverging from AOT (`OnPush`) for the app's own components. Here the JIT *declare* path (library partial declarations) diverges from the linker in the opposite direction: it applies the v22 default to declarations that predate v22. The two paths disagree with AOT in different ways, so fixing #70262 alone does not fix this. Expected: the JIT declare path applies the same rule as the linker, i.e. `OnPush` only when `decl.version` is >= 22 (or the placeholder version), `Eager` otherwise. Workaround we use in Storybook/Vitest (must run before any library declaration is evaluated): ```ts import '@angular/compiler'; import { ChangeDetectionStrategy } from '@angular/core'; const facade = (globalThis as any).ng?.ɵcompilerFacade; const original = facade.compileComponentDeclaration.bind(facade); facade.compileComponentDeclaration = (env: unknown, url: string, decl: any) => { const major = Number.parseInt(String(decl.version ?? '0').split('.')[0], 10); const patched = decl.changeDetection == null && major > 0 && major < 22 ? { ...decl, changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.Eager } : decl; return original(env, url, patched); }; ``` ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug https://github.com/diegohoyos/angular-jit-onpush-repro ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```true No exception. The component compiled through ɵɵngDeclareComponent gets ɵcmp.onPush === true and its view is never refreshed after the subscription assigns new state. ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```true Angular CLI : 22.2.0 Angular : 22.2.0 Node.js : 22.23.2 Package Manager : npm 12.0.2 Operating System : win32 x64 ┌───────────────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────────┐ │ Package │ Installed Version │ Requested Version │ ├───────────────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────────┤ │ @angular/build │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/cli │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/common │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/compiler │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/compiler-cli │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/core │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/platform-browser │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ rxjs │ 7.8.2 │ 7.8.2 │ │ typescript │ 6.0.3 │ 6.0.3 │ │ zone.js │ 0.16.3 │ 0.16.3 │ └───────────────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────────────────┘ The library (legacy-lib) was compiled with @angular/compiler-cli 20.3.33 / typescript 5.8.3, compilationMode: "partial". ``` ### Anything else? - `packages/compiler-cli/linker/.../partial_component_linker_1.ts`: `const hasOnPushByDefault = major >= 22 || version === PLACEHOLDER_VERSION;` then `changeDetection: metaObj.has('changeDetection') ? ... : hasOnPushByDefault ? OnPush : Eager`. - `packages/compiler/src/jit_compiler_facade.ts`, `convertDeclareComponentFacadeToMetadata`: `changeDetection: decl.changeDetection ?? ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` with no look at `decl.version`. - Reproduces on 22.0.x through 22.2.0.

Yes ### Description A library compiled with Angular < 22 in partial compilation mode (`ɵɵngDeclareComponent({ version: "20.3.x", ... })`) whose component omits `changeDetection` is handled differently by the two consumers of that declaration in an Angular 22 application: - **AOT (partial linker)** keeps it on `Default`/`Eager`: `packages/compiler-cli/linker/src/file_linker/partial_linkers/partial_component_linker_1.ts` computes `hasOnPushByDefault = major >= 22 || version === PLACEHOLDER_VERSION` and only then falls back to `OnPush`. That is correct: a component written for v20 was always checked and may assign state inside subscriptions or callbacks without `markForCheck()`. - **JIT (`ɵɵngDeclareComponent` → `ɵcompilerFacade.compileComponentDeclaration`)** ignores the declared version: `packages/compiler/src/jit_compiler_facade.ts`, `convertDeclareComponentFacadeToMetadata`, uses `changeDetection: decl.changeDetection ?? ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush`. The same v20 component becomes `OnPush` and silently stops re-rendering. JIT is what Storybook (`@storybook/angular`), Jest (`jest-preset-angular`), Vitest without the AOT plugin, `TestBed` and `ng serve --aot=false` use, so a library that works in the built application breaks in every one of those. We hit it with Kendo UI for Angular 25 (compiled with Angular 20.3): its internal `TreeViewGroupComponent` assigns nodes inside a subscription and rendered an empty tree in Storybook, while the AOT build was fine. This is the declare-path counterpart of #70262. That issue is about the JIT *decorator* path (`@Component` metadata → `Eager`) diverging from AOT (`OnPush`) for the app's own components. Here the JIT *declare* path (library partial declarations) diverges from the linker in the opposite direction: it applies the v22 default to declarations that predate v22. The two paths disagree with AOT in different ways, so fixing #70262 alone does not fix this. Expected: the JIT declare path applies the same rule as the linker, i.e. `OnPush` only when `decl.version` is >= 22 (or the placeholder version), `Eager` otherwise. Workaround we use in Storybook/Vitest (must run before any library declaration is evaluated): ```ts import '@angular/compiler'; import { ChangeDetectionStrategy } from '@angular/core'; const facade = (globalThis as any).ng?.ɵcompilerFacade; const original = facade.compileComponentDeclaration.bind(facade); facade.compileComponentDeclaration = (env: unknown, url: string, decl: any) => { const major = Number.parseInt(String(decl.version ?? '0').split('.')[0], 10); const patched = decl.changeDetection == null && major > 0 && major < 22 ? { ...decl, changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.Eager } : decl; return original(env, url, patched); }; ``` ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug https://github.com/diegohoyos/angular-jit-onpush-repro ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```true No exception. The component compiled through ɵɵngDeclareComponent gets ɵcmp.onPush === true and its view is never refreshed after the subscription assigns new state. ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```true Angular CLI : 22.2.0 Angular : 22.2.0 Node.js : 22.23.2 Package Manager : npm 12.0.2 Operating System : win32 x64 ┌───────────────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────────┐ │ Package │ Installed Version │ Requested Version │ ├───────────────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────────┤ │ @angular/build │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/cli │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/common │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/compiler │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/compiler-cli │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/core │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/platform-browser │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ rxjs │ 7.8.2 │ 7.8.2 │ │ typescript │ 6.0.3 │ 6.0.3 │ │ zone.js │ 0.16.3 │ 0.16.3 │ └───────────────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────────────────┘ The library (legacy-lib) was compiled with @angular/compiler-cli 20.3.33 / typescript 5.8.3, compilationMode: "partial". ``` ### Anything else? - `packages/compiler-cli/linker/.../partial_component_linker_1.ts`: `const hasOnPushByDefault = major >= 22 || version === PLACEHOLDER_VERSION;` then `changeDetection: metaObj.has('changeDetection') ? ... : hasOnPushByDefault ? OnPush : Eager`. - `packages/compiler/src/jit_compiler_facade.ts`, `convertDeclareComponentFacadeToMetadata`: `changeDetection: decl.changeDetection ?? ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` with no look at `decl.version`. - Reproduces on 22.0.x through 22.2.0. ### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

forms

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

When a child field uses `debounce()`, submitting the form can pass the action the child's old value instead of what the user typed.

`submit()` calls `markAsTouched()` on the form root. `markAsTouched()` flushes the pending debounced value only for the field it is called on. Descendants are marked as touched, but their pending values are not flushed.

This shows up when the user presses Enter inside a debounced input. The input keeps focus, so the value is still pending when the action runs. Clicking a submit button hides the bug, because the click blurs the input and flushes its value first.

```ts
readonly profileForm = form(
  this.model,
  (p) => {
    debounce(p.name, 'blur');
  },
  {
    submission: {
      action: async (f) => {
        console.log(f.name().value()); // "" after typing "Ada" and pressing Enter
      },
    },
  },
);
```

```html
<form [formRoot]="profileForm">
  <input [formField]="profileForm.name" />
  <button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>
```

Steps:

1. Type "Ada" in the input.
2. Press Enter while the input still has focus.

Expected: the action receives "Ada".
Actual: the action receives "", and the model still holds "".

A duration debounce such as `debounce(p.name, 500)` has the same problem if Enter is pressed before the duration elapses.

forms

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

When a child field uses `debounce()`, submitting the form can pass the action the child's old value instead of what the user typed.

`submit()` calls `markAsTouched()` on the form root. `markAsTouched()` flushes the pending debounced value only for the field it is called on. Descendants are marked as touched, but their pending values are not flushed.

This shows up when the user presses Enter inside a debounced input. The input keeps focus, so the value is still pending when the action runs. Clicking a submit button hides the bug, because the click blurs the input and flushes its value first.

```ts
readonly profileForm = form(
  this.model,
  (p) => {
    debounce(p.name, 'blur');
  },
  {
    submission: {
      action: async (f) => {
        console.log(f.name().value()); // "" after typing "Ada" and pressing Enter
      },
    },
  },
);
```

```html
<form [formRoot]="profileForm">
  <input [formField]="profileForm.name" />
  <button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>
```

Steps:

1. Type "Ada" in the input.
2. Press Enter while the input still has focus.

Expected: the action receives "Ada".
Actual: the action receives "", and the model still holds "".

A duration debounce such as `debounce(p.name, 500)` has the same problem if Enter is pressed before the duration elapses.

### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

forms

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

If the template renders a `formControlName` for a control that the `FormGroup` doesn't have, the error depends on the build:

- **Dev mode:** `Error: Cannot find control with path: 'Options -> 2'`, which is clear.
- **Production:** `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading '_rawValidators')`. It says nothing about forms or which control is missing, so it is hard to trace back to the template.

A real-world way to hit this: the template and the `FormGroup` are built from the same list but with two different filters. An item passes the template's filter but not the form's, so the template asks for a control that was never added.

Cause: `AbstractFormDirective.addControl()` passes the result of `this.form.get(dir.path)` on without checking it for `null`. In dev mode, a `ngDevMode`-only check in `setUpControlValueAccessor` catches it. That check is stripped from production builds, so the `null` control reaches `setUpValidators`, which uses it right away.

Expected: a clear, coded error in production too, instead of a bare `TypeError`.

https://github.com/arturovt/form-control-name-missing-control-repro

TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading '_rawValidators')

body_text:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

forms

### Description

Using [formField] removes support for angular and native (attr.) bindings for things like disabled, required, etc. I can work around the lack of required thanks to validateStandardSchema and using requiredness from something like zod for reusability. Disabled however, appears to be forced to do something like `disabled(...)` in the form schema management which I despise as a pattern.

It is often the case that forms of any complexity and/or using components across multiple forms should not have to copy/paste a block of disabled, required, etc. logic. Previously, it's encapsulated in the child component that knows how its inputs should be managed.

For example, in a child component - a checkbox that disables a sibling input. In this new world, I'd have to do something like tie the checkbox value into the form value for exposure at the root form schema level so the child component's path can disable the appropriate input. Then, if this is used in another form, I have to do the exact same thing and so on. Additionally, if that condition ever changes, I have to update X forms worth of disabled logic. Instead of being able to modularly define my component management, it's now all top loaded at each form level which is not maintainable (not to mention having to *find* each form that uses the respective path associated to said component).


### Proposed solution

I would like inputs to once again support [disabled] (and optionally other things like required, if for no reason other than consistency) while using [formField]. If the [disabled] value needs to be a (writable?) signal instead of a primitive so that you can facilitate automatically changing the [formField] disabled value and viceversa to the [disabled] value, I can live with that.

I suppose I could also live with just an easy way to programmatically set disabled on the fieldState via an effect although I think this is less than ideal since now we have to individually manage a lot of side effects that should be unnecessary.

### Alternatives considered

An alternative to this could in theory be a function per child component that encapsulates all the relevant logic (taking a partial form schema as an argument) but that's a lot more boilerplate that should absolutely not be necessary and also beings to become quite unmaintainable at scale when there are lots of adapter child components around various inputs.

### Description

Using [formField] removes support for angular and native (attr.) bindings for things like disabled, required, etc. I can work around the lack of required thanks to validateStandardSchema and using requiredness from something like zod for reusability. Disabled however, appears to be forced to do something like `disabled(...)` in the form schema management which I despise as a pattern.

It is often the case that forms of any complexity and/or using components across multiple forms should not have to copy/paste a block of disabled, required, etc. logic. Previously, it's encapsulated in the child component that knows how its inputs should be managed.

For example, in a child component - a checkbox that disables a sibling input. In this new world, I'd have to do something like tie the checkbox value into the form value for exposure at the root form schema level so the child component's path can disable the appropriate input. Then, if this is used in another form, I have to do the exact same thing and so on. Additionally, if that condition ever changes, I have to update X forms worth of disabled logic. Instead of being able to modularly define my component management, it's now all top loaded at each form level which is not maintainable (not to mention having to *find* each form that uses the respective path associated to said component).

I would like inputs to once again support [disabled] (and optionally other things like required, if for no reason other than consistency) while using [formField]. ### Describe the problem that you experienced

The guide says a resource that reads only ctx.queryParams()['category'] should not reload when another query key (e.g. sort) changes.
In @angular/router 22.2.0, this does not hold if the read is inline inside resource({ params }):
```
// Reloads when *any* query param changes (including `sort`)
byCategory: resource({
  params: () => ctx.queryParams()['category'] ?? 'all',
  loader: ({ params }) => api.fetchByCategory(params),
}),
```
`ctx.queryParams()` is one signal for the whole object. Any query change re-runs params, so the resource reloads even when 'category' is unchanged.

A workaround that actually worked for me:
```
const category = computed(() => ctx.queryParams()['category'] ?? 'all');

byCategory: resource({
  params: category,
  loader: ({ params }) => api.fetchByCategory(params),
}),
```

I have built a demo app where I experimented with all this new resource options, you'll find this use case there: https://stackblitz.com/~/github.com/famzila/angular-route-resource-demo

body_text:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

`core`, `platform-server`

### Is this a regression?

No known unaffected version; I did not identify an introduction commit.

### Description

An Angular SSR application that displays user-submitted rich text through a normal `[innerHTML]` binding can spend several seconds synchronously parsing a small, deeply nested HTML article. The server-side sanitizer creates a Domino `template`, assigns the untrusted HTML to `template.innerHTML`, and reads it back during its stability check. With 8,000 well-nested `<div>` levels, the pinned Domino parser overflows the stack in `recursivelySetOwner()`.

The reproduction accepts an unauthenticated Markdown submission (184 KB, below its 1 MiB limit). Marked 18.0.11 preserves the raw HTML, and an ordinary `AngularNodeAppEngine` request renders the stored article. It does not use `bypassSecurityTrustHtml`, a private parser API, modified Angular packages, or direct server state changes. `optimization.styles.inlineCritical` is set to `false` to isolate this sanitizer path from critical-CSS processing.

Expected: sanitization either renders or rejects an over-deep article without a long synchronous worker stall.

Actual: the article GET returns HTTP 200 with an empty article after a stack error; another request arriving at the same single-worker server during parsing waits behind it. The stored article triggers the same error on later GETs. The Node process stays alive.

In a fresh Linux arm64 container with Node 24.21.0 and released Angular 22.2.0 packages:

| Input (fresh worker each) | Article GET | Unrelated GET started 2 s later | Outcome |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 184 KB shallow, same byte count | 644 ms | 14 ms | Article rendered; no stack error |
| 184 KB, 8,000 levels plus inner children, run 1 | 10,025 ms | 8,017 ms | Empty article; `RangeError` |
| Same nested input, run 2 | 10,097 ms | 8,091 ms | Empty article; `RangeError` |

This demonstrates a repeatable single-worker availability problem and article render failure. It does not establish a process crash or multiworker service outage. The application must accept raw HTML in lower-trust content and render it on SSR; applications that strip raw HTML, limit depth, or do not SSR that content are outside this path.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

https://github.com/BlueIridium-Security/angular-ssr-nested-html-worker-stall-repro

The repository has a pinned package lock and a one-command Docker validator:

```sh
docker build -t angular-ssr-nested-html-repro .
docker run --rm angular-ssr-nested-html-repro
```

The validator starts a new server for each case, sends the article through HTTP, measures a concurrent unrelated request, checks the empty-vs-rendered article, and requires the Domino stack error in both nested runs.

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```text
RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
```

The generated server log maps this stack to Domino's recursive owner assignment. The request is caught by the SSR renderer, which returns a 200 page with an empty article.

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in

### Is this a regression?

No known unaffected version; I did not identify an introduction commit.

### Description

An Angular SSR application that displays user-submitted rich text through a normal `[innerHTML]` binding can spend several seconds synchronously parsing a small, deeply nested HTML article. The server-side sanitizer creates a Domino `template`, assigns the untrusted HTML to `template.innerHTML`, and reads it back during its stability check. With 8,000 well-nested `<div>` levels, the pinned Domino parser overflows the stack in `recursivelySetOwner()`.

The reproduction accepts an unauthenticated Markdown submission (184 KB, below its 1 MiB limit). Marked 18.0.11 preserves the raw HTML, and an ordinary `AngularNodeAppEngine` request renders the stored article. It does not use `bypassSecurityTrustHtml`, a private parser API, modified Angular packages, or direct server state changes. `optimization.styles.inlineCritical` is set to `false` to isolate this sanitizer path from critical-CSS processing.

Expected: sanitization either renders or rejects an over-deep article without a long synchronous worker stall.

Actual: the article GET returns HTTP 200 with an empty article after a stack error; another request arriving at the same single-worker server during parsing waits behind it. The stored article triggers the same error on later GETs. The Node process stays alive.

In a fresh Linux arm64 container with Node 24.21.0 and released Angular 22.2.0 packages:

| Input (fresh worker each) | Article GET | Unrelated GET started 2 s later | Outcome |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 184 KB shallow, same byte count | 644 ms | 14 ms | Article rendered; no stack error |
| 184 KB, 8,000 levels plus inner children, run 1 | 10,025 ms | 8,017 ms | Empty article; `RangeError` |
| Same nested input, run 2 | 10,097 ms | 8,091 ms | Empty article; `RangeError` |

This demonstrates a repeatable single-worker availability problem and article render failure. It does not establish a process crash or multiworker service outage. The application must accept raw HTML in lower-trust content and render it on SSR; applications that strip raw HTML, limit depth, or do not SSR that content are outside this path.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

https://github.com/BlueIridium-Security/angular-ssr-nested-html-worker-stall-repro

The validator starts a new server for each case, sends the article through HTTP, measures a concurrent unrelated request, checks the empty-vs-rendered article, and requires the Domino stack error in both nested runs.

body_text:
### Describe the problem that you experienced

The landing page frames most of the tradeoffs/nuance in forms as template vs reactive forms. Signal forms are condensed to a singular sentence: "TIP: If you're looking for the new Signal Forms, check out our [essential Signal Forms guide](https://angular.dev/essentials/signal-forms)!"

### Enter the URL of the topic with the problem

https://angular.dev/guide/forms

### Describe what you were looking for in the documentation

I would assume that these days, the Overview would more likely be one of the following

- A balance of all three. Like the signal forms subpage comparing all three form APIs: https://angular.dev/guide/forms/signals/comparison. In fact, IMO that page could stand in for the bulk of the existing Overview.
- Signal forms first with template/reactive forms given a brief overview, and then relevant links to their respective sections. Like the following:
    - [Reactive forms overview](https://angular.dev/guide/forms/reactive-forms)
    - [Template driven forms overview](https://angular.dev/guide/forms/template-driven-forms).
    - The [aforementioned comparison page](https://angular.dev/guide/forms/signals/comparison) subsection of the signal forms docs
    - ["Migrating existing forms to Signal Forms"](https://angular.dev/guide/forms/signals/migration) subsection of the signal forms docs
    - The existing Overview page as it is now is still a good page. It would make for a good standalone page for legacy forms consideration.

### Describe the actions that led you to experience the problem

Going to the forms main section from the root of the docs

### Describe what you want to experience that would fix the problem

IMO the [signal forms comparison vs reactive/template page](https://angular.dev/guide/forms/signals/comparison) copy could be the new forms Overview page. And to combine both my points above from "Describe what you were looking for in the documentation", I would say that the Overview should be a mix of both points: the comparison page but signal forms first, and then links to relevant pages for the legacy forms APIs and to the existing Overview copy as its own non-default forms overview page.

### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? core, platform-server (the pinned Domino HTML parser) ### Is this a regression? No. ### Description **Security impact: SSR availability.** When an application renders lower-trust HTML through a normal `[innerHTML]` binding during server-side rendering, one element with many *distinct* attributes can occupy a Node.js worker for seconds. The sanitizer eventually removes those attributes, but Domino parses them first. An attacker who can submit such content and request its page can delay otherwise valid requests served by the same worker. In a two-worker deployment, one stored article and one GET per worker delayed valid requests to both workers for about 20 seconds. The current Angular `main` lockfile pins Domino commit `1929b1ef5aee03234de322c5bbd955ba653d8727`. In that revision, [`handleSimpleAttribute()`](https://github.com/angular/domino/blob/1929b1ef5aee03234de322c5bbd955ba653d8727/lib/HTMLParser.js#L2336-L2365) scans every previously parsed attribute name before appending a new one. [`addAttribute()`](https://github.com/angular/domino/blob/1929b1ef5aee03234de322c5bbd955ba653d8727/lib/HTMLParser.js#L2320-L2333) does the same. A single element with distinct names therefore causes quadratic name-comparison work. Angular's [SSR HTML sanitizer](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/439d495aaa53ebce35e46464a08b5fb10a5ecd61/packages/core/src/sanitization/html_sanitizer.ts#L304-L333) constructs and reparses an inert document before it can strip the attributes. Minimal input generator: ```js const html = ` ` a${i}="x"`).join('')}>x`; // 538,902 UTF-8 bytes; 50,000 distinct, nonnumeric attribute names. ``` To reproduce the lower-trust path, accept this as a submitted Markdown article with raw HTML enabled (for example, Marked 18.0.11), then render the parsed article in a generated Angular SSR page containing `
`. The tested app used `AngularNodeAppEngine` and `REQUEST_CONTEXT`; it did not use `bypassSecurityTrustHtml`, a custom sanitizer, or a patched framework. The submission cap was 1 MiB. `POST /submit` stored the article; `GET /article` triggered SSR. The attacker can make that GET without waiting for another reader. On an exact-main production build, Node v24.21.0, macOS arm64, default heap and stack settings, and `optimization.styles.inlineCritical: false`: | 538,902-byte input | Article GET | Valid benign POST started 2 s later | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Same-size plain HTML text, one worker | 22 ms | 6 ms | | 50,000 duplicate attributes with size-matched filler, one worker | 38 ms | 2 ms | | 50,000 distinct attributes, fresh worker 1 | 11,405 ms | 9,403 ms | | 50,000 distinct attributes, fresh worker 2 | 12,714 ms | 10,710 ms | | Same-size plain HTML text, two workers | 23 / 72 ms | 4 / 4 ms | | 50,000 distinct attributes, two workers | 21,999 / 21,902 ms | 19,996 / 19,901 ms | All article requests returned 200, all benign POSTs returned 201, and the workers survived. The attack response contained sanitized `
x
`; the raw attributes did not survive. The benign POST handler does not parse the stored article, so its delay reflects worker unavailability rather than additional processing of the attack input. The HTTP reproduction used Angular main `7d96a37af4f7b7dd9dc9a2b9b90cc043c7da2a31` and CLI main `564d6d83151b993c4d6825f91fcac033470a35f6`. On 2026-10-06, Angular main had advanced to `439d495aaa53ebce35e46464a08b5fb10a5ecd61`; the Domino pin, sanitizer, inert-document helper, and Domino adapter remained unchanged. Released Angular 22.2.0 also showed the stall in a separate run. This requires an application workflow that accepts substantial raw HTML from a lower-trust actor and SSR renders it through `[innerHTML]`. Sites that reject raw HTML or cap attribute counts do not have the demonstrated path. The observed consequence is worker starvation, not a process crash or a demonstrated outage of every deployment. ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug Standalone released-package reproduction: https://github.com/BlueIridium-Security/angular-ssr-attribute-parser-stall-repro It contains the SSR app, pinned npm lockfile, same-byte controls, and a validator. Run `npm ci`, `npm run build`, and `npm run validate` on supported Node 24.x. The input generator, path, and measured controls are also summarized above. ### Please provide the exception or error you saw No exception. The worker remained alive but could not promptly serve another valid request while sanitizing the article. ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) Angular core and platform-server built from `7d96a37af4f7b7dd9dc9a2b9b90cc043c7da2a31`; Angular CLI/SSR built from `564d6d83151b993c4d6825f91fcac033470a35f6`; Domino pin `1929b1ef5aee03234de322c5bbd955ba653d8727`; Node v24.21.0; macOS 26.6.2 arm64. A released Angular 22.2.0 run provided secondary evidence. ### Anything else? This is distinct from #70826 (numeric attribute sparse storage), #70926 (active-formatting reconstruction), and #71195 (deep-tree owner recursion). The input here is a well-formed single `
` with distinct nonnumeric names. Avoiding repeated linear scans of preceding names, or otherwise bounding parser work per element, would address the observed cost.

body_text: ### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request? router ### Description `NavigationBehaviorOptions` got a `scroll` option in a03c82564d (#64417, for #26744), so a single navigation can opt out of scrolling. It works with `router.navigate()` and `router.navigateByUrl()`, but `RouterLink` has no matching input, so it can't be used from a template. Where I ran into it: tabs driven by a query param (`?tab=reviews`) further down a page, with `withInMemoryScrolling({scrollPositionRestoration: 'top'})`. Every click on a tab jumps back to the top of the page. #26744 is locked now, but it has plenty of the same cases (a `page` param for infinite scroll, a `?sidebar` param, an auxiliary route opening a modal), and most of those navigations start from a link rather than from code. It also matters for the Navigation API integration: `extras.scroll` is what the router passes to `NavigateEvent#intercept({scroll})`, and a navigation started by a `RouterLink` has no way to set it. `RouterLink` already forwards `skipLocationChange`, `replaceUrl`, `state`, `info` and `browserUrl` (the last one was added for #66805). `scroll` isn't forwarded yet. ### Proposed solution A `scroll` input on `RouterLink`, typed from `NavigationBehaviorOptions['scroll']` and passed to `router.navigateByUrl` with the other extras: ```html Reviews ``` #70963 implements this the same way `browserUrl` was added: the key is only put in the extras when the input is set, so navigations from links that don't use it are unchanged. ### Alternatives considered - Replacing the link with a `(click)` handler that calls `router.navigate(..., {scroll: 'manual'})`. That gives up the `href` (no ctrl/cmd+click, no "open in new tab", no link semantics for screen readers) and `routerLinkActive`. - The workarounds people posted in #26744 before the option existed: a fragment that doesn't match anything on the page, a dynamic getter on `scrollPositionRestoration`, or `location.replaceState` to bypass the router. They all still apply to links today.

body_text:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? core ### Is this a regression? No (same code on `main` today) ### Description With `provideClientHydration(withIncrementalHydration(), withEventReplay())`, a `@defer (hydrate on viewport)` block containing a `routerLink` anchor loses any click that lands after the viewport trigger has started hydration but before it finishes. The jsaction contract captures the click and calls `preventDefault()`, so the browser does not navigate either. The event is queued for replay but never replayed, and once hydration completes the `jsaction` attribute is removed. The user clicks a link and nothing happens. The same click works if it is the first thing to trigger hydration (before the viewport trigger fires), and after hydration has finished. Only the in-flight window is affected. That window is the lazy chunk fetch plus the block's first render, so it is a few ms on localhost, hundreds of ms on a mobile connection or a throttled CPU, and it opens exactly when the user has just scrolled the content into view. Any non-replay trigger has the same effect (`viewport`, `idle`, `timer`, `immediate`, `when`, a parent block hydrating), because the cause is in how a second hydration request is handled: 1. `hydrateAndInvokeBlockListeners` (`packages/core/src/hydration/event_replay.ts`) pushes the event onto `EVENT_REPLAY_QUEUE` and calls `triggerHydrationFromBlockName(injector, blockName, replayFn)`. 2. `triggerHydrationFromBlockName` (`packages/core/src/defer/triggering.ts`) sees the block in `dehydratedBlockRegistry.hydrating` and returns immediately, dropping `replayFn`. 3. The in-flight hydration was started by `setViewportTriggers` with no replay function, so `triggerHydrationForBlockQueue` never drains the queue (`if (replayQueuedEventsFn) { replayQueuedEventsFn(hydrationQueue); }`). 4. `cleanupHydratedDeferBlocks` removes `jsaction` / `ngb` from the block's elements. The event stays in the queue forever. A fix could be either of: - in the early-return path, attach the replay to the in-flight hydration, e.g. `blocksBeingHydrated.get(blockName).promise.then(() => replayQueuedEventsFn?.([blockName]))`, or - have `triggerHydrationForBlockQueue` always drain the shared queue for the blocks it hydrated, regardless of which trigger started it. ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug https://github.com/stones/angular-incremental-hydration-click-replay (a fresh `ng new repro --ssr` with the files below, plus `probe.cjs`) Changes over the CLI scaffold: - `app.config.ts`: `provideClientHydration(withIncrementalHydration(), withEventReplay())`, `provideRouter(routes, withEnabledBlockingInitialNavigation())`. - `app.routes.ts`: `''` → `HomeComponent`, `'target'` → `TargetComponent` (renders "TARGET PAGE"). - `app.routes.server.ts`: `{ path: '**', renderMode: RenderMode.Server }`. - `home.component.ts`: a 3000px spacer, then `@defer (hydrate on viewport) { } @placeholder {

placeholder

}`. - `slow-section.component.ts`: standalone, imports `RouterLink`, template `Go to target`; `onClick` logs `handler ran`. Steps: ``` npm install npm run build NG_ALLOWED_HOSTS=localhost PORT=4017 node dist/repro/server/server.mjs ``` 1. Open `http://localhost:4017/`. In DevTools, throttle the network to "Slow 3G" so the chunk fetch is long enough to click inside. 2. Scroll the link into view. The IntersectionObserver fires and the `slow-section` chunk is requested. 3. Click "Go to target" while the chunk is still loading. 4. Nothing happens. The URL stays `/`, `handler ran` is never logged, and when the chunk arrives the anchor's `jsaction` attribute is gone. Controls: `document.getElementById('link').click()` from the console before scrolling navigates (replay triggers hydration and is replayed). Clicking after the chunk has loaded navigates. Automated: `node probe.cjs 5 50,300,800 dom,mouse 1000` runs the three scenarios in Playwright Chromium with 1000 ms of artificial latency on the lazy chunk. Results on 22.0.8: | Scenario | runs | navigated | handler ran | `jsaction` stripped after click | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | click before the viewport trigger fires | 15 | 15 | 15 | 0 | | click during hydration (50 / 300 / 800 ms after scroll) | 40 | **0** | **0** | **40** | | click after hydration finished | 25 | 25 | 25 | 0 | Both `element.click()` and a real `page.mouse.click()` behave the same. ### Please provide the exception or error you saw No error. The click is silently dropped. ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in ``` Angular CLI: 22.0.9 Node: 24.18.0 Package Manager: npm OS: win32 x64 @angular/core 22.0.8 (also common, router, platform-browser, platform-server) @angular/ssr 22.0.9 @angular/build 22.0.9 ``` ### Anything else? Separate observation, possibly its own issue or docs gap: with the CLI default `provideRouter(routes)` (non-blocking initial navigation) the `hydrate on viewport` trigger in this app never registers. `withIncrementalHydration()`'s `APP_BOOTSTRAP_LISTENER` runs `runIncrementalHydrationBootstrap`, which is a no-op until `ɵɵenableIncrementalHydrationRuntime()` has run, and the compiler emits that call in the create block of the first template containing a hydrate block, which the router has not rendered when bootstrap finishes. The repro uses `withEnabledBlockingInitialNavigation()` to get past this.

### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

router

---

### Description

`withViewTransitions()` currently triggers a view transition on every router navigation regardless of the user's `prefers-reduced-motion` setting. When the browser supports the View Transitions API, the router always calls `document.startViewTransition()`, and the browser plays at least its default root cross-fade. This happens even for users who have asked their operating system to reduce motion.

Relevant code: [`createViewTransition()` in `packages/router/src/utils/view_transition.ts`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/packages/router/src/utils/view_transition.ts). The function decides whether to run `startViewTransition()` based only on browser support (`document.startViewTransition`) and `skipNextTransition`. There is no check against `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')`.

`prefers-reduced-motion` is not a capability fallback (that part is already handled: unsupported browsers degrade to a plain DOM update). It is a deliberate user accessibility preference, often set for vestibular/motion sensitivity reasons. Treating it as the default opt-out is in line with WCAG guidance (SC 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions) and with how the platform itself frames the preference.

A developer *can* already honor the preference today via the `onViewTransitionCreated` callback and `transition.skipTransition()` (current workaround):

```typescript
withViewTransitions({
  onViewTransitionCreated: ({ transition }) => {
    if (matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) {
      transition.skipTransition();
    }
  },
})
```

But this is opt-in boilerplate that most developers won't know they need. The accessible behavior should be the default, following the principle of progressive enhancement: motion is the enhancement layered on top of a working, accessible baseline and not something each team has to remember to switch off.

The View Transitions integration (`withViewTransitions()` / `ViewTransitionsFeatureOptions`) is still marked `@developerPreview`, so changing the default behavior now carries essentially no ecosystem cost, so IMO now is a good point of time where the default behavior can be changed.

Note: there is a prior related issue, [#52571 — *docs: support prefers-reduced-motion in View Transitions API*](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/52571), but it was scoped to the angular.dev **website** and closed on the basis that the API already makes it *possible* to respect the preference. This request is different: it asks for the framework to make respecting the preference the **default behavior** of `withViewTransitions()`, not merely possible. A maintainer reference for the mechanism is linked in that thread: [Reacting to the reduced-motion preference (Chrome docs)](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/view-transitions/#reacting-to-the-reduced-motion-preference).

---

### Proposed solution

Make `withViewTransitions()` skip the transition by default when `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` is `true`, while still performing the DOM update (the navigation). Concretely, in `createViewTransition()` short-circuit before calling `document.startViewTransition()` when reduced motion is requested — the same way `skipNextTransition` is handled today — so neither Angular's own named transitions nor the browser's default root cross-fade run.

Add an option to `ViewTransitionsFeatureOptions` to control this, defaulting to the accessible behavior, e.g.:

```typescript
export interface ViewTransitionsFeatureOptions {
  skipInitialTransition?: boolean;
  onViewTransitionCreated?: (transitionInfo: ViewTransitionInfo) => void;

  /**
   * Whether to skip the view transition when the user has requested reduced
   * motion via `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. The DOM update (navigation)
   * still runs; only the animation is skipped.
   *
   * @default true
   */
  skipTransitionOnReducedMotion?: boolean;
}
```

- Default `true`: accessible out of the box.
- Teams that have a reason to keep animating (and provide their own reduced-motion-safe animations) can set it to `false`.
- Media-query evaluation should be guarded so it is a no-op on the server / where `matchMedia` is unavailable.

**On the breaking-change question:** this is a behavior change, but a small and
defensible one, and arguably a bug fix rather than a breaking change:

- The API is `@developerPreview`, so it is explicitly not covered by SemVer stability guarantees.
- The current behavior arguably violates the user's expressed accessibility preference, so changing it is closer to fixing a defect than removing a feature.
- The visible effect of the new default only materializes for users who have `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` set — i.e. exactly the users who asked for less motion.

---

### Alternatives considered

1. **Keep it opt-in via `onViewTransitionCreated` (status quo).** Works, but leaves the accessible behavior as hidden boilerplate most teams never add, so real apps ship motion to users who opted out. Rejected as the default.

2. **Conditionally register `withViewTransitions()` at bootstrap** by checking `prefers-reduced-motion` first (mirrors the old `NoopAnimationsModule`/`BrowserAnimationsModule` split suggested in [#52571](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/52571)). This reads the preference only once at startup and does not react to changes, requires the developer to wire it up, and spreads config logic into bootstrap. Less ergonomic than a sensible default.

3. **Document the `onViewTransitionCreated` + `skipTransition()` pattern only, without changing the default.** Better than nothing, but documentation does not change the default experience; accessibility defaults should be safe, not something you read your way into.

4. **CSS-only mitigation** (`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` around all custom keyframes). This disables the author's own animations but does **not** stop the browser's default root cross-fade that `startViewTransition()` triggers, so motion still reaches the user. It is a complement, not a substitute, for skipping the transition at the API level.

---

### Willing to contribute

I'd be happy to work on this myself and open a PR (changes to `createViewTransition()` and `ViewTransitionsFeatureOptions`, plus tests and docs). Before I start, I'd like to confirm with the team whether the proposed direction — making reduced-motion skipping the default, with an opt-out option — is acceptable, and whether you'd prefer a different API shape or naming. Happy to adjust based on your guidance.

{"repository": "angular/angular", "task_candidate_id": 119, "repository_id": 9, "issue_number": 71345, "github_issue_id": 5843193334, "html_url": "https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/71345", "created_at": "2026-10-14T06:39:30+00:00", "author_association": "CONTRIBUTOR", "title": "feat(router): respect `prefers-reduced-motion` by default in `withViewTransitions()`", "body_text": "### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

router

---

### Description

`withViewTransitions()` currently triggers a view transition on every router navigation regardless of the user's `prefers-reduced-motion` setting. When the browser supports the View Transitions API, the router always calls `document.startViewTransition()`, and the browser plays at least its default root cross-fade. This happens even for users who have asked their operating system to reduce motion.

Relevant code: [`createViewTransition()` in `packages/router/src/utils/view_transition.ts`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/packages/router/src/utils/view_transition.ts). The function decides whether to run `startViewTransition()` based only on browser support (`document.startViewTransition`) and `skipNextTransition`. There is no check against `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')`.

`prefers-reduced-motion` is not a capability fallback (that part is already handled: unsupported browsers degrade to a plain DOM update). It is a deliberate user accessibility preference, often set for vestibular/motion sensitivity reasons. Treating it as the default opt-out is in line with WCAG guidance (SC 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions) and with how the platform itself frames the preference.

A developer *can* already honor the preference today via the `onViewTransitionCreated` callback and `transition.skipTransition()` (current workaround):

```typescript
withViewTransitions({
  onViewTransitionCreated: ({ transition }) => {
    if (matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) {
      transition.skipTransition();
    }
  },
})
```

But this is opt-in boilerplate that most developers won't know they need. The accessible behavior should be the default, following the principle of progressive enhancement: motion is the enhancement layered on top of a working, accessible baseline and not something each team has to remember to switch off.

The View Transitions integration (`withViewTransitions()` / `ViewTransitionsFeatureOptions`) is still marked `@developerPreview`, so changing the default behavior now carries essentially no ecosystem cost, so IMO now is a good point of time where the default behavior can be changed.

Note: there is a prior related issue, [#52571 — *docs: support prefers-reduced-motion in View Transitions API*](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/52571), but it was scoped to the angular.dev **website** and closed on the basis that the API already makes it *possible* to respect the preference. This request is different: it asks for the framework to make respecting the preference the **default behavior** of `withViewTransitions()`, not merely possible. A maintainer reference for the mechanism is linked in that thread: [Reacting to the reduced-motion preference (Chrome docs)](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/view-transitions/#reacting-to-the-reduced-motion-preference).

---

### Proposed solution

Make `withViewTransitions()` skip the transition by default when `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` is `true`, while still performing the DOM update (the navigation). Concretely, in `createViewTransition()` short-circuit before calling `document.startViewTransition()` when reduced motion is requested — the same way `skipNextTransition` is handled today — so neither Angular's own named transitions nor the browser's default root cross-fade run.

Add an option to `ViewTransitionsFeatureOptions` to control this, defaulting to the accessible behavior, e.g.:

```typescript
export interface ViewTransitionsFeatureOptions {
  skipInitialTransition?: boolean;
  onViewTransitionCreated?: (transitionInfo: ViewTransitionInfo) => void;

  /**
   * Whether to skip the view transition when the user has requested reduced
   * motion via `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. The DOM update (navigation)
   * still runs; only the animation is skipped.
   *
   * @default true
   */
  skipTransitionOnReducedMotion?: boolean;
}
```

- Default `true`: accessible out of the box.
- Teams that have a reason to keep animating (and provide their own reduced-motion-safe animations) can set it to `false`.
- Media-query evaluation should be guarded so it is a no-op on the server / where `matchMedia` is unavailable.

**On the breaking-change question:** this is a behavior change, but a small and
defensible one, and arguably a bug fix rather than a breaking change:

- The API is `@developerPreview`, so it is explicitly not covered by SemVer stability guarantees.
- The current behavior arguably violates the user's expressed accessibility preference, so changing it is closer to fixing a defect than removing a feature.
- The visible effect of the new default only materializes for users who have `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` set — i.e. exactly the users who asked for less motion.

---

### Alternatives considered

1. **Keep it opt-in via `onViewTransitionCreated` (status quo).** Works, but leaves the accessible behavior as hidden boilerplate most teams never add, so real apps ship motion to users who opted out. Rejected as the default.

2. **Conditionally register `withViewTransitions()` at bootstrap** by checking `prefers-reduced-motion` first (mirrors the old `NoopAnimationsModule`/`BrowserAnimationsModule` split suggested in [#52571](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/52571)). This reads the preference only once at startup and does not react to changes, requires the developer to wire it up, and spreads config logic into bootstrap. Less ergonomic than a sensible default.

3. **Document the `onViewTransitionCreated` + `skipTransition()` pattern only, without changing the default.** Better than nothing, but documentation does not change the default experience; accessibility defaults should be safe, not something you read your way into.

4. **CSS-only mitigation** (`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` around all custom keyframes). This disables the author's own animations but does **not** stop the browser's default root cross-fade that `startViewTransition()` triggers, so motion still reaches the user. It is a complement, not a substitute, for skipping the transition at the API level.

---

### Willing to contribute

I'd be happy to work on this myself and open a PR (changes to `createViewTransition()` and `ViewTransitionsFeatureOptions`, plus tests and docs). Before I start, I'd like to confirm with the team whether the proposed direction — making reduced-motion skipping the default, with an opt-out option — is acceptable, and whether you'd prefer a different API shape or naming. Happy to adjust based on your guidance.

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

As said in https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/65756, the FormUiControl doesn't allow the inputs to have type-altering transforms.
A similar problem arises for min/max inputs.

body_text: ### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request? core ### Description Hey team. Currently, errors occurring within `computed/linkedSignal` lack any information about the nature of the error itself in the prod: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/92e5aa8f154096a756757d0e295cde4299788650/packages/core/primitives/signals/src/computed.ts#L136 As a result, the error signature in Sentry is uninformative, making it impossible to determine where an error originated without examining the stack traces: Furthermore, when errors arise from different locations (for instance, from `computed` and `linkedSignal`) it becomes difficult to distinguish between them in Sentry’s error lists (though Sentry’s built-in grouping mechanism does [at least separate them](https://docs.sentry.io/concepts/data-management/event-grouping/#grouping-by-stack-trace)), which complicates the process of locating and debugging errors. ### Proposed solution For each error, add a code instead of a message, as has already been done for `RuntimeError` ### Alternatives considered I know why [it has been done](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/44210#pullrequestreview-810615849), but maybe it is possible to simplify (shorten) error messages in all modes and remove the `ngDevMode` at all.

### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

core

### Description

Proposes a fix for #68937.

`npx skills add https://github.com/angular/skills` copies the skill for the latest Angular version, and the copy does not change when the project upgrades. Shipping the skill in `@angular/core` keeps the skill and the framework at the same version, and `ng update` updates both.

Version alignment is the stated goal of shipping skills in npm packages ([skills-npm proposal](https://github.com/antfu/skills-npm/blob/main/PROPOSAL.md), [skills-npm#33](https://github.com/antfu/skills-npm/issues/33)). Tools that link `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` from `node_modules` into agent skill directories:

- **pnpm** 12.11.0 ([docs](https://pnpm.io/agent-skills), [RFC pnpm/rfcs#35](https://github.com/pnpm/rfcs/pull/35)): `pnpm install` links skills of direct dependencies after `pnpm approve`.
- **`npx skills experimental_sync`** in skills v1.7.4 ([docs](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/docs/commands.md#skills-experimental_sync), RFC [vercel-labs/skills#2323](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/2323)): links skills of installed dependencies, for any package manager. Usually run from `prepare`.
- **[antfu/skills-npm](https://github.com/antfu/skills-npm)**: same approach, being merged into the `skills` CLI.
- **vlt**: `vlt skills` / `--allow-skills` ([vltpkg/vltpkg#1983](https://github.com/vltpkg/vltpkg/pull/1983)), merged, not released yet.

### Proposed solution

Ship `skills/dev-skills/angular-developer` as `skills/angular-developer/` in `@angular/core`, via a filegroup in the `ng_package` `srcs`, like `resources/best-practices.md`.

- One level deep (`skills/<name>/SKILL.md`), which pnpm requires. No `package.json` field needed.
- Leave out `angular-new-app`, which is used before `@angular/core` is installed.

```
# pnpm
$ pnpm approve
# -> .claude/skills/pnpm-@angular+core-angular-developer -> node_modules/@angular/core/skills/angular-developer

# npm / yarn
$ npx skills experimental_sync -y
# -> .agents/skills/angular-developer -> node_modules/@angular/core/skills/angular-developer
```

### Concerns

- **Download size**: every install, including CI and production builds, downloads the skill (about 60 KB gzipped, about 4% of the 1.57 MB `@angular/core` tarball). Raised in [antfu/skills-npm#32](https://github.com/antfu/skills-npm/issues/32) and [npm/cli#9222](https://github.com/npm/cli/issues/9222), without a resolution.
- **No standard**: npm distribution is not in the Agent Skills spec ([agentskills/agentskills#81](https://github.com/agentskills/agentskills/issues/81) was closed as not planned). `experimental_sync` is experimental.
- **pnpm install failures**: after approval, `pnpm install` fails when no agent skill directory exists, for example in a Docker build that does not copy `.claude/` ([pnpm/pnpm#16744](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/16744)).
- **Duplicates**: users who ran `npx skills add` would have two copies for possibly different versions.
- **Overlap** with `resources/best-practices.md`.

### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? compiler-cli ### Is this a regression? Yes The previous version in which this bug was not present was: 17.0.0 ### Description Template references can't be reassigned, but nothing stops you from doing it in an event binding: ```html

Hello

Bye

 ``` The compiler doesn't report anything, with or without `strictTemplates`. What happens next depends on how the app is built: - With the CLI's application builder, the build fails in esbuild, on the generated code. The error points at line 21 of a 14-line file, at a name I never wrote (full output below). - In JIT, the click silently does nothing. The JIT output declares the reference with `var`, so the assignment only overwrites a local variable. - If the AOT output runs without going through esbuild (I loaded it directly in Node with jsdom), the click throws `TypeError: Assignment to constant variable.` 17.0.0 rejected the same template at compile time: ``` Cannot assign value "bye" to template variable "hello". Template variables are read-only. ``` From what I can tell, that check lived in TemplateDefinitionBuilder and went away with it. The template semantics checker reports writes to template variables (`let-x`, `@for` items, `as` aliases) with NG8005, but it only looks at `TmplAstVariable`, so references aren't covered. The type-check block declares references with `var` too, so TypeScript only complains when the assigned value has an incompatible type. The more likely way to run into this is a reference that shadows a component property, like `` with `(click)="query = ''"` in a component that has a `query` field. With `strictTemplates` you get `Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'HTMLInputElement'`, which at least fails, if confusingly. Without it, you're back to the cases above. I wasn't sure whether leaving references out of that check was on purpose, so I'm starting with an issue. If it wasn't, reporting them next to variables with the same error looks like a small change in `template_semantics_checker.ts` and in its copy in the preprocessor. I have it on a branch with tests. ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug No hosted reproduction, but a fresh CLI app with this component shows it: ```ts import {Component} from '@angular/core'; import {NgTemplateOutlet} from '@angular/common'; @Component({ selector: 'app-root', imports: [NgTemplateOutlet], template: `

Hello

Bye

 `, }) export class App {} ``` ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```true Application bundle generation failed. ✘ [ERROR] Cannot assign to "hello_r2" because it is a constant src/app/app.ts:21:225: 21 │ ....ɵɵreference(3); return i0.ɵɵresetView(hello_r2 = bye_r3); }); ╵ ~~~~~~~~ The symbol "hello_r2" was declared a constant here: src/app/app.ts:21:123: 21 │ ...ɵɵrestoreView(_r1); const hello_r2: any = i0.ɵɵreference(1)... ╵ ~~~~~~~~ ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```true Angular CLI 22.2.1 (application builder), @angular/compiler-cli 22.2.1. Same on 22.3.0-next.2 and main (d0b33ad25f). Rejected at compile time on 17.0.0. ``` ### Anything else? _No response_

### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

router

### Is this a regression?

No (same on 21)

### Description

All related functions, to my knowledge, except `createUrlTreeFromSnapshot`, allow removing specific parameters from URLs by specifing their keys with null-ish value, eg.:

```
this.router.navigate(['./'], { queryParams: { hello: null } });
```

Above would remove "hello" query parameter when executed.

The `createUrlTreeFromSnapshot` however behaves differently:

```
 this.router.navigateByUrl(
    createUrlTreeFromSnapshot(this.activatedRoute.snapshot, [], {
      hello: null,
    })
  );
```

Above would set "hello" query parameter to "null" (so ?hello=null).

This is especially perplexing, given constructing URL tree manually works just fine:

```
this.router.navigateByUrl(
    this.router.createUrlTree(['/'], { queryParams: { hello: null } })
);
```

above would also clear the "hello" key.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-yphtdp7t?file=src%2Fmain.ts

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```true

```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```true
Angular 22
```

### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? Don't known / other ### Is this a regression? Yes ### Description # Angular issue: an early click makes a prerendered `target="_blank"` link permanently unclickable (stale `__jsaction` cache) **Package:** `@angular/core` (event replay / incremental hydration) **Version:** 22.2.3 (reproduced on a fresh `ng new --ssr` project; first seen after upgrading an app from 19 to 22) **Browser:** Chrome (stable) ## Description With the v22 default `provideClientHydration()` (incremental hydration, which brings event replay), a prerendered `` that is clicked while event replay is still active becomes **permanently unclickable**. Every later click is `preventDefault()`ed by the event contract, even after Angular has removed the `jsaction` attribute. No new tab opens until the page is reloaded. Clicking only after the app is stable works. Using `withNoIncrementalHydration(), withEventReplay()` also works. ## Minimal reproduction `ng new repro --ssr --routing --defaults` (Angular 22.2.3), then replace three files: `src/app/app.ts` ```ts import { Component, PendingTasks, inject } from '@angular/core'; import { RouterLink, RouterOutlet } from '@angular/router'; @Component({ selector: 'app-root', imports: [RouterLink, RouterOutlet], template: ` Open /other in a new tab `, }) export class App { constructor() { // Stand-in for an HTTP request in flight after load: keeps the app unstable for 3 s. inject(PendingTasks).run(() => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 3000))); } } ``` `src/app/other.ts` ```ts import { Component } from '@angular/core'; @Component({ selector: 'app-other', template: `

Other page

` }) export class Other {} ``` `src/app/app.routes.ts` ```ts import { Component } from '@angular/core'; import { Routes } from '@angular/router'; import { Other } from './other'; @Component({ selector: 'app-home', template: `

Home page

` }) class Home {} export const routes: Routes = [ { path: '', component: Home }, { path: 'other', component: Other }, ]; ``` `app.config.ts` stays as generated: `provideClientHydration()`. Build (`ng build`, prerender), serve `dist/repro/browser` statically, open `/`. ## Steps 1. Within the first ~3 s (app bootstrapped, not yet stable), click "Open /other in a new tab". 2. Wait until the app is stable; the `jsaction` attribute disappears from the link. 3. Click the link again. **Expected:** step 3 opens `/other` in a new tab. **Actual:** nothing happens. The click is `preventDefault()`ed by the event contract; this repeats on every click until reload. Control cases (same app, real trusted clicks): | Configuration | Early click, then click at 6 s | Clicks only at 6 s and 8 s | |---|---|---| | `provideClientHydration()` (v22 default) | **6 s click: no tab** (`defaultPrevented=true`) | both open a tab | | `provideClientHydration(withNoIncrementalHydration(), withEventReplay())` | both open a tab | both open a tab | Stack of the `preventDefault()` on the 6 s click (dev build): `Dispatcher.dispatch` → `EventDispatcher.dispatch` → `_EventContract.dispatcher` → `_EventContract.handleEventInfo` → `_EventContract.handleEvent` → listener on ``. ## Root cause (from the 22.2.3 sources) 1. On the early click, `ActionResolver.parseActions(element)` parses `jsaction="click:;"` and caches the parsed map **on the element** as the property `element.__jsaction` (`set(actionElement, actionMap)`). 2. When the block/app is cleaned up, `removeListeners(el)` does `el.removeAttribute('jsaction'); el.removeAttribute('ngb'); el.__jsaction_fns = undefined;` but it **does not clear `el.__jsaction`**. 3. With incremental hydration enabled, the `EventContract` is not cleaned up after `whenStable()`. `withEventReplay`'s bootstrap listener only calls `eventContract.cleanUp()` on app destroy when `isIncrementalHydrationEnabled`, so the `` listener stays active. 4. On every later click, `parseActions` returns the stale cached map, so an action is found. Because the element is an `` and the event is a click, `shouldPreventDefaultBeforeDispatching` returns true and the default (opening the new tab) is cancelled. RouterLink then leaves `target="_blank"` to the browser, so nothing navigates. Without the early click, `__jsaction` was never cached; after the attribute is removed `parseActions` sees no attribute, and the click is not prevented. With incremental hydration off, the contract is cleaned up at stable, so the stale cache is never consulted. Same-tab `routerLink`s mask the problem (RouterLink navigates itself after the default is prevented); any anchor that relies on the browser default (`target="_blank"`, plain `href` with a `(click)` listener, download links) is affected. ## Workaround we use An inline script at the end of `index.html` removes `jsaction` from `a[target="_blank"]` before any click, so these links are never intercepted or cached: ```html ``` ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug _No response_ ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```true ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```true Angular CLI : 22.2.3 Angular : 22.2.3 Node.js : 24.21.0 Package Manager : npm 11.19.0 Operating System : darwin arm64 ``` ### Anything else? _No response_

### Reproduction link

[https://stackblitz.com/edit/aruv3qkn-w8zgqdcz?file=src%2Fdemo.tsx](https://stackblitz.com/edit/aruv3qkn-w8zgqdcz?file=src%2Fdemo.tsx)

### Steps to reproduce

The font size of Space.Addon does not respect the theme’s Input.fontSize setting.

In our project, we customized the theme by setting component  Input.fontSize to 12px. However, the text rendered inside Space.Addon remains at 14px and does not inherit the configured font size.

In contrast, when using addonBefore or addonAfter on Input, the font size correctly follows the parent Input’s fontSize, resulting in consistent typography.

This leads to inconsistent text sizing between Space.Addon and other Input addons.


### What is expected?

Space.Addon should inherit the component Input.fontSize value from the theme, just like addonBefore and addonAfter.

### What is actually happening?

Space.Addon text is always rendered at 14px (token.fontSize) , ignoring the Input fontSize theme configuration.

### What problem does this feature solve?


### 🐛 问题描述

在 antd v4.x 及更高版本中，`RangePicker` 的左右两个面板默认是**联动**的。当用户修改左侧面板的年份或月份时，右侧面板会自动跳转到左侧时间之后的月份。

虽然这个设计在选择较短的连续时间范围时比较方便，但当需要选择**跨度较大的时间范围**时，操作体验非常差。

### 📌 具体痛点

例如我想选择 **2020 年 到 2026 年** 这样一个跨度较大的范围：

- 我把左侧面板调整到 2020 年
- 右侧面板会自动跳到 2021 年甚至更后面
- 我需要反复点击箭头很多次，才能把右侧面板调整到 2026 年

操作非常繁琐，低效。

而在 antd 3.x 版本中，左右面板是相对独立的，调整左侧不会影响右侧，这种场景下使用更方便。

### ✅ 期望收益

- 显著提升选择大跨度时间范围时的用户体验
- 兼容历史项目（默认行为不变）
- 让 `RangePicker` 更灵活，满足不同业务场景的需求（报表、数据分析、历史记录等）



### What does the proposed API look like?

### 💡 建议方案

希望6.x官方能增加一个属性，让开发者可以**自主控制是否开启面板联动**，例如：

```tsx
<RangePicker 
  unlinkPanels={true}           // 或 independentPanels={true}
/>
```

或者更语义化的写法：

```tsx
<RangePicker 
  panelMode="independent"       // 默认值为 "linked"
/>
```

这样既能保留现有默认行为（联动），又能让需要大跨度选择的用户获得更好的体验。

### Reproduction link

[![Edit on CodeSandbox](https://codesandbox.io/static/img/play-codesandbox.svg)](https://codesandbox.io/p/devbox/clever-agnesi-42g4tx?workspaceId=ws_UJWDJFW6u5eT5bSdmMxLcC)

### What is expected?

At least one of the following should be supported:

Option A — Pass autoComplete directly as a prop to `<Select>`:
`<Select autoComplete="new-password" />`

Option B — Pass a custom <Input> element with autoComplete via `children`:
`<Select><Input autoComplete="new-password" /></Select>`

(The components.input path in Input.js already supports React elements via cloneElement and merges existingProps on top of sharedInputProps — but antd does not expose this components.input override publicly.)

### What is actually happening?

Any autoComplete prop passed to <Select> ends up on the outer wrapper <div>, not the <input>. The underlying input always receives autoComplete="off".

| Environment | Info |
| --- | --- |
| antd | 6.4.3 |
| React | 19.2.1 |
| System | Windows 11 |
| Browser | Latest Chrome |

---
With `AutoComplete`, it is possible to pass a child Input component, which allows setting native HTML props such as autoComplete directly on the underlying input element:

```
<AutoComplete>
  <Input autoComplete="off" />
</AutoComplete>
```

However, with `Select`, there seems to be no equivalent way to pass custom props (e.g. autoComplete) to the inner input element. Is there a supported API for this, or would it be possible to add something like an inputProps or styles/classNames extension that also covers native input attributes?

[![Edit on CodeSandbox](https://codesandbox.io/static/img/play-codesandbox.svg)](https://codesandbox.io/p/devbox/clever-agnesi-42g4tx?workspaceId=ws_UJWDJFW6u5eT5bSdmMxLcC)

### What is expected?

At least one of the following should be supported:

Option A — Pass autoComplete directly as a prop to `<Select>`:
`<Select autoComplete="new-password" />`

Option B — Pass a custom <Input> element with autoComplete via `children`:
`<Select><Input autoComplete="new-password" /></Select>`

(The components.input path in Input.js already supports React elements via cloneElement and merges existingProps on top of sharedInputProps — but antd does not expose this components.input override publicly.)

### What is actually happening?

With `AutoComplete`, it is possible to pass a child Input component, which allows setting native HTML props such as autoComplete directly on the underlying input element:

```
<AutoComplete>
  <Input autoComplete="off" />
</AutoComplete>
```

However, with `Select`, there seems to be no equivalent way to pass custom props (e.g. autoComplete) to the inner input element. Is there a supported API for this, or would it be possible to add something like an inputProps or styles/classNames extension that also covers native input attributes?
